correctness.rationale: The homogeneous Jacobian is solved exhaustively in three disjoint coordinate cases. It has one isolated singular point at t=0 and 8+16=24 at t=1, with no other critical parameters. Exact symbolic Groebner remainders prove the equation, gradient and Hessian determinant (3456 or 3456*rho^2) at all nodes. The smooth quartic tangent cone is proved by its partials. Standard hypersurface results yield Milnor number 27, exceptional genus 3, discrepancy -2 and E^2=-4; Euler specialization gives 28 and 31. Verified by running the newly embedded SymPy checker, not extrapolated from finite numeric samples.

originality.rationale: The precise exceptional parameter set is explicitly proved in Yu–Zhu Lemma 3.1 and is excluded from the originality claim. Their original full accessible HTML was checked, particularly Section 3.1 and later sections; it does not give the 24-node configuration, the ordinary quadruple-point resolution and associated Milnor and Euler data. Focused published-finding corpus searches with full equation and aliases identified no stronger or equivalent singularity-basket theorem. Similarity to another ordinary quadruple point is object-specific coincidence, not implication. Historical priority remains provisional because not all older published literature was exhausted.

value.rationale: The twenty-four isolated nodes versus one nonrational ordinary 4-fold boundary are natural, complete degenerations of a record-rich 85-line quintic pencil. Exact singularity baskets and Euler defects provide concrete input for studying specialization of line configurations and geometry of the pencil; they are not merely a numerical example or a renamed smoothness criterion.
